samples.summary: Substantial scope beyond the stated issue (#661). The branch's own task doc says it "carries two bodies of work: its stated scope (#661 — the CLI error envelope as one line carrying `command`) and a CLI login-hardening epic". On top of that epic, this diff also lands three further, independent subsystems: a new backend `Secure`-cookie predicate (`useSecureCookies`, `COOKIE_SECURE` env var, `oauth-state.ts:184-207`), a brand-new access-log redaction module (`packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts`, 184 lines + spec + backend.md/rest-api.md sections), and a frontend login-form error-map rewrite (`login-form.tsx`). None of these is required by the error-envelope outcome, and each is separately reviewable/revertable. A reviewer cannot approve the #661 acceptance criteria without also accepting an auth-cookie policy change and a log-redaction policy change. Recommend splitting; at minimum the issue/PR body needs to state which criteria each body of work satisfies.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present as described. The quoted task-doc line is verbatim at docs/tasks/active/20260820-pr786-conflict-resolution-todo.md:8-10. The #661 acceptance criteria (docs/tasks/active/20260811-cli-error-envelope-command-todo.md:56-63) are limited to single-line envelope, `command` attribution, and unchanged code/message. Yet the change also carries: (1) a backend Secure-cookie predicate `useSecureCookies()` reading `COOKIE_SECURE` (oauth-state.ts:185,205), consumed at auth.controller.ts:373 and cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:61, with new spec cases and design-doc prose (backend.md:426,437); (2) a new access-log redaction module packages/backend/src/logging/log-safe-url.ts (174 lines) wired at app.module.ts:23,70 with a full spec and doc sections (backend.md:490-491, rest-api.md:550); (3) a Map-based login error-map in packages/frontend/src/components/login-form.tsx:26-51. None of these serves the error-envelope outcome, so approving #661's criteria also means approving an auth-cookie policy change and a log-redaction policy change — squarely the "unrequested scope creep" this lens is told to flag, and a scope/fit violation rather than a taste preference. The finding's only inaccuracies are cosmetic and non-refuting: log-safe-url.ts is 174 not 184 lines, and logSafeUrl/COOKIE_SECURE are part of the login-hardening epic (per 20260812-cli-login-loopback-binding-todo.md:126,154,161-164) rather than layered on top of it. No refutation ground applies: nothing is absent, nothing is unreachable, and scope creep is explicitly in this lens's lane.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. docs/design/backend.md:708 does add an `OAUTH_STATE_SECRET` row to the canonical Environment Configuration table claiming the OAuth login bindings are "signed with" a key that, when unset, is "derived from JWT_SECRET with a fixed label" (HKDF); packages/backend/README.md:25-34 repeats the HKDF claim. No code implements it: repo-wide grep for OAUTH_STATE_SECRET hits only those two doc lines plus .agent-review artifacts, and grep for STATE_SECRET|hkdf|HKDF under packages/backend/src returns no matches. packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:1 imports only createHash/randomBytes/timingSafeEqual; the web state is randomBytes(32) plus unkeyed SHA-256 (lines 120-123, 132-140, 221-223), and the reusing caller cli-auth.store.ts:62,104 uses the same unkeyed hash. The only keyed constructions in backend src are unrelated (yorkie-signature.guard.ts:53 webhook secret; cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:103 HMAC keyed by the cookie secret itself). This is in-lane design-doc discipline: the canonical subsystem doc must describe the system as built (docs filed by validity per CONTRIBUTING), and documenting a non-existent operator knob in the Environment Configuration table is a real fit violation, not a taste preference. No guard or alternate spelling makes it unreachable or true.

verdict.reason: The absence claim is false: docs/design/backend.md:437-441, inside the Cookie Configuration section (:379-:460), explicitly records the new knob — "`COOKIE_SECURE=true` is the escape hatch for a TLS-terminating edge in front of an `http://` callback URL, which would otherwise downgrade the session cookie too" — mirroring the implementation rationale at packages/backend/src/auth/oauth-state.ts:180-182. The canonical design doc was therefore updated, not skipped, and the knob is folded into the correct subsystem doc rather than a parallel file. The finding's cited code evidence is also wrong for this repository: packages/backend/src/auth/github-auth.guard.ts contains no `secure`/`COOKIE_SECURE` reference at all; the precedence (COOKIE_SECURE -> GITHUB_CALLBACK_URL scheme -> NODE_ENV) lives in oauth-state.ts:184-195, exported as useSecureCookies() at :205-207. Residual imprecision does exist — the summary paragraph at backend.md:381-388 omits the COOKIE_SECURE branch and names the predicate `secureCookies`, and the env table at :702-721 has no COOKIE_SECURE row (NODE_ENV row at :717 still calls itself the fallback) — but the design-fit rubric's major bar is a missing or parallel/duplicate design doc, and neither applies. An absent table row plus an intro summary of a rule fully stated 50 lines below in the same section is documentation polish (minor/nit), which never blocks.
